text:
amelia: FYI my PR #342 just turned the CI red — pre-commit/typecheck gate failing. Can't reproduce the failure locally yet. Anyone able to quick triage? :grimacing:

ci-bot: CI failed for PR #342 — jobs: pre-commit (typecheck) failed. Log: https://ci.internal/redwood/342 (logs attached) :warning:

sam: paste the top of the pyright/mypy output? usually it's a tiny signature mismatch we can patch.

amelia: here's the failing snippet from the job log:
```
inference/runner.py:218:21 - error: Argument of type "RunnerConfig | None" cannot be assigned to parameter "cfg" of type "RunnerConfig" in function "initialize_runner"
  Type "None" cannot be assigned to type "RunnerConfig". (reportGeneralTypeIssues)
```
I added an optional `config` to Runner earlier in the PR, maybe my change exposed a stricter rule.

marina: can you run `pre-commit run --all-files`? pyright runs inside pre-commit so local run should match CI.

amelia: ran it — can't repro, pre-commit passes locally for me. Maybe CI is using a newer pyright config on main?

raj: last green on main was at 1768599000. We landed a change to `pyrightconfig.json` in main earlier today (tighten `reportGeneralTypeIssues`). That could explain why your PR fails in CI but not locally if you haven't pulled main. Try rebasing on main and running the typecheck hook.

sam: also check pre-commit pinned versions: `pre-commit autoupdate` was run in main yesterday, CI uses the updated hooks. If you have an older `.cache/pre-commit`, local may still pass. Run:
```
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
pre-commit run --all-files
```

ci-bot: CI artifact excerpt:
```
pyright: 1.1.362
pyrightconfig.json: {
  "reportGeneralTypeIssues": true
}
```

marina: I rebased amelia's branch and ran pre-commit, reproduced the error. Quick minimal stack: `RunnerConfig` is Optional in the signature of `start()` but `initialize_runner` expects non-optional. Patch idea: update `initialize_runner` to accept `RunnerConfig | None` and handle defaulting, or make the callsite assert non-null.

sam: prefer minimal change: if PR already has the optional there, add an assert/guard where you call `initialize_runner`:
```
if config is None:
    config = RunnerConfig.default()
initialize_runner(config)
```
That keeps types happy without lowering config strictness.

amelia: I can push that now. Would it be acceptable to temporarily add `# type: ignore` on the call to get CI green while we debate the right approach?

raj: avoid `type: ignore` unless fixing the underlying logic is tricky. This is small, add the guard. Thanks.

amelia: pushed a small fix in #343 with the guard + unit test for defaulting. Can someone kick off a rerun?

ops-bot: Rerun requested by amelia on PR #343 — job queue position 4.

ci-bot: Rerun started: pre-commit (typecheck).

marina: quick heads-up — if CI still fails after the guard, it might be because pyright on CI uses a newer setting that flags implicit `default()` return types. If so we'll fold a tiny type annotation on `RunnerConfig.default() -> RunnerConfig` in the same PR.

ci-bot: Rerun finished — all checks passed :tada: (pre-commit / typecheck green).

sam: nice! thanks for the quick turnaround.

amelia: thanks everyone — closing the loop. will watch for any followups if the stricter pyright flags catch other places. :slightly_smiling_face:
